title: Wren and the Postcard
premise: Marine biologist Casper Blackwood retreats to a windswept island research station after a betrayal by his former partner and mentor, Dr. Vivian Ashford, who stole credit for his life's work on sea turtle migration. A community pen-pal program meant for tourists accidentally pairs him with a stranger who turns out to be Wren Calloway — Vivian's estranged daughter and a journalist investigating her mother's misconduct. Through anonymous letters and postcards they fall for each other without knowing identities; when the truth surfaces mid-season, loyalty to family collides with truth-telling, forcing both to choose between protecting the people who hurt them and the story that could set them free. The novel ends as Casper forgives himself for staying silent too long, exposes nothing but testifies honestly at last, and boards the final ferry of the season with Wren beside him.
about_author: Emrys Dunmore is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper turned novelist who writes love stories set where the land runs out of road. Their work is known for salt-bleached prose, slow-burning tension, and endings that feel earned rather than given.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He arrives at Greywater Island for the nesting season, cataloguing turtles like a man counting anything but heartbreaks. Flashbacks reveal Vivian Ashford published his migration data under her own name. Emotional beat: numbness mistaken for peace, and a vow that the heart is just a trainable muscle.

chapters.title: The Pen-Pal Program
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The island's tourism board assigns researchers anonymous pen pals to humanize science outreach. Casper signs up out of obligation. His first letter is dry, clinical. The reply he receives back is sharp, funny, and refuses to be impressed. Beat: reluctant curiosity cracking the ice.

chapters.title: Wren Comes Ashore
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Journalist Wren Calloway arrives on the ferry under a false surname, chasing a source about her mother Vivian's fraudulent research. She doesn't know her assigned pen pal works at the very station she's investigating. Beat: guilt braided with determination.

chapters.title: Letters Like Tide Charts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV via letters. The pen pals trade confessions disguised as small talk: fear of becoming one's parents, the loneliness of being believed in only for what you produce. Neither knows how close to home they're striking. Beat: intimacy without faces.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the station open house, Wren sees Casper's desk photo — him and Vivian, younger, triumphant. Her stomach drops: her pen pal knew her mother intimately. She says nothing. Beat: first secret, first self-betrayal.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A storm strands Wren at the station overnight. They argue about scientific ethics in the abstract — she testing him, he defending a position he no longer believes. Sparks fly, hostile and magnetic. Beat: enemies made flesh, attraction denied.

chapters.title: Postcard from the Edge
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren mails an unsigned postcard confessing something true to her pen pal — that she's terrified of loving anyone connected to her mother's sins. Casper reads it on the beach and feels seen for the first time in years. Beat: vulnerability as turning point.

chapters.title: Vivian Visits
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Vivian arrives unannounced to 'check on her investment' in the station. Casper swallows his anger over dinner while Wren watches her mother charm the room. Beat: power performing itself; old wounds reopened.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After a night surveying hatchlings, Casper and Wren nearly kiss on the dunes. Both pull back — he because of loyalty to a dead friendship, she because of the lie she's living. Beat: desire checked by duty, twice.

chapters.title: The Source Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's whistleblower contact delivers documents proving Vivian falsified data — and that Casper was the original author. She now holds the proof that would vindicate her pen pal and destroy her mother. Beat: loyalty vs. truth becomes literal.

chapters.title: What the Letters Knew
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Rereading his pen pal's letters, Casper recognizes phrasing from Wren's storm-night argument. He realizes who she is — and that she's been investigating him. Beat: betrayal felt before it's confirmed; the mirror cracks.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Casper confronts Wren on the tidal flats: journalist, daughter, liar. She fires back that he hid behind anonymity too. They say unforgivable, accurate things. Beat: climax of the middle; love and fury indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Silence Is Also a Choice
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Alone, Casper admits his real sin wasn't losing credit — it was staying silent for years to protect his career. He drafts a resignation letter he can't send. Beat: the enemy in the mirror named.

chapters.title: Mother's Draft
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Vivian discovers Wren's investigation and pleads — then threatens — invoking family loyalty. Wren must decide whether blood is a debt or an excuse. Beat: the corrupting pull of inherited power made personal.

chapters.title: Hatchling Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. During the season's biggest hatchling release, Casper and Wren work side by side in wordless truce, guiding turtles to the sea. No apologies yet, but hands brush. Beat: tenderness surviving wreckage.

chapters.title: The Ferry Manifest
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns Vivian plans to publish again — building fraud atop fraud — and that the station's funding depends on complicity. Deadline pressure mounts: the exposé must run before the last ferry. Beat: ticking clock engaged.

chapters.title: Confession in the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Casper tells Wren the full truth unprompted — every year he stayed silent, every compromise. It's not absolution he asks for but witness. Beat: forgiveness of self begins by being fully seen.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Wren's story breaks naming Vivian and crediting Casper's original work. Vivian calls Wren a traitor; Casper publicly confirms everything. The island takes sides. Beat: truth costs exactly what it's worth.

chapters.title: Ashes and Salt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the aftermath, Wren grieves the mother she wished she had. Casper finds her on the beach and doesn't fix anything — just sits with her until dawn. Beat: love as presence, not rescue.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The final ferry approaches. Casper has been offered a prestigious mainland post built on his restored name — and Wren is leaving for her next assignment. Both pretend the decision isn't a decision. Beat: the choice deferred to breaking point.

chapters.title: One More Postcard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the dock, Casper hands Wren a postcard — the confession he should have written years ago, addressed to himself, forwarded to her. She reads it, laughs, cries. He declines the mainland post. Beat: forgiveness completed; the muscle retrained.

chapters.title: Departures
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They board the last ferry together — not fleeing, but choosing a season that moves. Epilogue beat: months later, a postcard arrives at the station from two names signed as one. The tide, like the heart, always comes back.
